name: Britannia Industries Ltd
title: Britannia Industries Ltd - 500825 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q4 FY26 consol sales +7.1% to INR 4,686 cr with PAT +21% helped by tax case releases; domestic growth ~9-9.5% ex dual-pricing and West Asia, with price hikes and no capacity-discipline signal.

summary.headline: Britannia Q4 FY26 revenue rose 7.1% to INR 4,686 crore, with PAT up 21.1% to INR 678 crore helped by a tax case release.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue was INR 4,686 crore (+7.1% YoY) and FY26 revenue was INR 18,858 crore (+7.5%). Q4 PAT of INR 678 crore (+21.1%) was lifted by income tax case closures, so underlying profit growth was weaker. Management attributed the India slowdown in March to dual pricing of INR 5 and INR 10 packs after the GST transition, which hit wholesale and rural channels, plus West Asia disruption to international dispatches. Management guided to price increases from this quarter to offset fuel and laminate inflation.

financial_highlights.change: +21.1% YoY; 14.5% of revenue; boosted by income tax case releases

segments.name: Domestic India
segments.commentary: Growth was about 9% to 9.5% in Q4 before dual-pricing drag; management said it expects a few hundred bps of lost sales to recover. Retail (75% of business) is growing well, while wholesale (25%) was hit.

segments.name: E-commerce
segments.commentary: E-commerce was 6% of domestic sales in FY26 versus 4% in FY25, and management put it above 12% excluding the INR 5 and INR 10 packs. Quick commerce is about 70% of e-commerce, which management expects to reach 85%.

segments.name: International (West Asia)
segments.commentary: Revenue and profitability were hit in Q4 by vessel unavailability through the Strait of Hormuz and weaker demand in West Asia markets. Management said the business was negative for March, and Oman production for North America has moved back to Mundra.

segments.name: Adjacencies and signature brands
segments.commentary: Wafers are growing at healthy double digits and dairy at double digits, led by ghee. Treat, Little Hearts and Jim Jam are growing about 3x company growth, and cake and rusk is growing about 1.4x biscuits.

guidance_outlook: Calibrated price increases start from Q1 FY27, through grammage adjustments and some packs above INR 10.
Management expects the domestic market to stabilize by quarter-end as dual pricing fades, and expects wholesale and rural volumes to recover.
Sourcing optimisation between India and international plants is expected to be fully operational by mid-May 2026.
Management expects biscuit industry sequential growth to resume from June with monsoon and school reopening.
Management is committed to continued cost efficiency programmes (CEP) and plans to step up advertising and brand investment, with no quantified FY27 margin guidance.
No specific FY27 revenue or margin number was given; management said it is confident of a good year.
capex_capacity: Manufacturing for North America was moved from Oman back to Mundra, enabling dispatch to North America.
Management is evaluating alternate fuels and energy sources as long-term hedges against fuel supply shocks.
Renewable electricity share in own plants rose 14%, and specific water consumption fell 7%.
Management did not announce new capacity or capex figures.
demand_pricing: Dual pricing of INR 5 and INR 10 packs (competitor selling at INR 4.5 and INR 9) hit rural and wholesale channels from January through March; the 60-65% of biscuits sold at these price points are most exposed.
Management said the gap is about 200 to 400 bps in sales, but it cannot precisely quantify the impact.
Price realisation on the INR 5 and INR 10 segment is lower than the competitor's, so management believes value share is unaffected.

Raw material view: wheat is deflationary but has risen over the past month on rains and quality; palm oil is covered for 5 months; sugar stable; cocoa lower; laminate and fuel (LPG, CNG) are inflationary.
Wheat inventory is covered for about 5.5 to 6 months at attractive prices; palm oil is covered for 5 months.
Other expenses rose 18% on 7% revenue growth, driven by higher advertising and brand investment.

qa_highlights.question: Why was standalone growth lower in Q4 when Nov-Dec ran at about 12% and Jan-Feb at about 9%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the first two months of Q4 were reasonable, with dual pricing in rural and wholesale channels hitting throughout the quarter, and West Asia pulling March down. Domestic growth was about 9% to 9.5% before the dual-pricing drag.

qa_highlights.question: How much did dual pricing dampen sales growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was hypothetical to quantify, but the impact was roughly 200 to 400 bps. Growth in general trade key accounts is high-single to double digit, modern trade is about 15% to 16%, and e-commerce is above 50%.

qa_highlights.question: What pricing action is needed given competitors are vacating INR 4.5 and INR 9 packs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will take selective price increases through grammage adjustments and some packs above INR 10. Other biscuit companies are moving gradually to full price points.

qa_highlights.question: Is Britannia under-indexed on INR 5 and INR 10 packs in e-commerce?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not actively promote these packs online because premium packs drive more value and channel conflict is a concern. The packs remain available through search and in baskets.

qa_highlights.question: Will GST cut benefits reach biscuits, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the GST benefit is less visible on INR 5 and INR 10 packs than on higher price points. It expects benefits to show more in medium to long term, with the growth recovery in June.

qa_highlights.question: What is Q4 volume growth and how do pack counts look?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume growth was about 5.5% by grammage. It acknowledged that transactions fell in wholesale and rural channels and expects this to correct over the next few months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook for FY27 given cost pressures and higher investment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will be selective on marketing spend, targeting the marketing mix for better returns, and expects to manage margins within a certain band. No quantified FY27 margin guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company pursue inorganic growth and new platforms?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is actively scanning acquisitions that add new capabilities or address unmet needs, and that more platforms will be added, including health.

risks_watch: Recovery of dual-pricing-hit wholesale and rural channels and whether the INR 5 and INR 10 price points normalise.
Q4 PAT includes income tax case releases, so the reported 21.1% PAT growth is not recurring.
Fuel and laminate inflation, plus West Asia shipping and LPG constraints, could pressure margins and international operations.
Competitor (number 2 player) reported double-digit volume growth, which may signal share loss in INR 5 and INR 10 channels.
Rising other expenses (+18% YoY) from brand investment could weigh on margins in FY27.
Price increases could affect volumes, which management argues will remain resilient.
summary.management_tone: Confident on medium-term recovery and cost discipline, but cautious and sometimes vague on near-term numbers. Management avoided quantifying the dual-pricing impact and FY27 guidance, and said the outcome depends on execution.
key_quotes: So, there will be calibrated price increases starting from this quarter.
And we are very confident that in very short period of time, these channels will also come back to normalcy.
So we had a volume growth of close to 5.5% upwards.
I think we have to keep going stronger on market share, but like we said that we are also adept at managing margins.

growth.why: No FY27 revenue or margin number was given; management guided to calibrated price increases from Q1 FY27 and expects domestic stabilisation and wholesale/rural recovery by quarter-end, with biscuit sequential growth resuming from June, but these are not backed by quantified capacity or orders.
